extra.message: Message content is rendered with the '| safe' filter in the admin messages view. Messages are stored via the unauthenticated API endpoint MessagesView.post (api/views.py:43-56, which has no @admin_required decorator) and via send_feedback (account_area/views.py:61-78). An attacker can submit a message containing JavaScript that executes in the administrator's browser when the admin views the messages page (stored XSS), enabling admin account compromise.

extra.message: The 'next' query parameter is read from user input via request.args.get('next') and passed directly to Flask's redirect() without any validation or allow-listing. An attacker can craft a URL such as /toggle_xss_protection/?next=https://evil.com to redirect users to an arbitrary external site (open redirect), useful for phishing and session-token theft.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: The Flask SECRET_KEY is hardcoded as 'Keep it secret, keep it safe'. Flask uses this key to cryptographically sign session cookies; anyone who knows it can forge a valid session cookie for any user (including the admin), bypassing authentication entirely. The key is also committed to source control.

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key

extra.message: DEBUG mode is explicitly enabled (app.config['DEBUG'] = True). Running Flask in debug mode exposes the Werkzeug interactive debugger, which can permit remote code execution if the debugger PIN is derived or bypassed, and leaks sensitive application internals and stack traces on errors.

cwe: CWE-215: Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Debugging Code

extra.message: The add_admin management command defaults the administrator password to 'admin' (def add_admin(password='admin')). The README instructs users to run 'python manage.py add_admin', so the application commonly runs with the trivially guessable admin/admin credentials, enabling authentication bypass.

User passwords are stored in plaintext (password = db.Column(db.String(200))) and compared directly with '==' in login/views.py:17 (user.password == password); no hashing/salting is performed anywhere (including change_password, which stores new_password verbatim). The Flask-Admin AdminOnlyModelView(User) also displays these plaintext passwords. A database compromise exposes all credentials in cleartext.

cwe: CWE-256: Plaintext Storage of a Password
CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information

extra.message: The publicly accessible login page renders the text 'Use credentials "admin/admin" to log in as admin', disclosing valid administrator credentials to every unauthenticated visitor and directly enabling unauthorized administrative access.
